title: Warm and cool spring slopes of honeysuckle leaf-to-bloom intervals had no clear common difference in US records from 1968 to 2004
abstract: We tested whether the temperature slope of the time from first leaf to first bloom differed between cool and warm springs in two honeysuckle clones. We used 5,160 site-species-years at 284 US sites from 1968 to 2004. A continuous two-slope model held site-species effects, year effects and January-February temperature fixed. The pooled warm minus cool slope was -0.85 days per C, with a 95% interval from -2.20 to +0.51. The early western estimate was negative, but the later western estimate changed sign. Neither clone nor all four region-period tests gave clear evidence after correction for their test families. The data do not establish a common slope difference or equal slopes. Unknown visits, selected complete records, coarse monthly weather and sparse later records limit inference. This study does not test air pollution or a causal climate effect. The package preserves code, source events, weather, source hashes, results, a figure and a separate coefficient check.

display.caption: Warm minus cool slope of the leaf-to-bloom interval. Bars give individual 95% intervals with site and year clusters. The early western result did not repeat in the later western period. These intervals have no adjustment across tests.
